name: h470skills
author: h410m-h
description: Curated master collection of Google Antigravity (AGY) core skills, power-user capabilities, full-stack playbooks, and codebase memories.

core-agy.title: Google Antigravity Core & Builtin Skills
core-agy.description: Official builtin Antigravity capabilities, customizations, guides, automations, and plugins.

skills.name: agy-customizations
skills.description: Google Antigravity (agy): comprehensive reference for the Antigravity Customization System — rules, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, and JSON configs, with their loading priority and discovery roots. Use when the user asks how Antigravity customizations work or load, or wants to create or debug an Antigravity skill, rule, plugin, hook, or MCP server configuration.

skills.name: antigravity-guide
skills.description: Provides a comprehensive guide, quick reference, and sitemap for Google Antigravity (AGY), including the Antigravity CLI (agy), Antigravity 2.0, Antigravity IDE, Python SDK, slash commands, keybindings, and customizations (skills, rules, MCP, sidecars). Activate this skill when the user asks questions about how to use, configure, or customize Antigravity, AGY, the agy CLI, the Antigravity IDE, or Antigravity 2.0.

skills.name: automation
skills.description: Google Antigravity (agy) only: interactive guide to design and create a scheduled background automation with Antigravity's automation/sidecar tools. Use when the user, working inside Antigravity, wants an automated or recurring scheduled task (e.g. "summarize my emails every morning", "every Monday send me a to-do list"), or types /automation. Not for Claude Code scheduled tasks, cron on a server, or CI schedules.

skills.name: generative-ui
skills.description: Google Antigravity (agy) only: how to render rich interactive HTML widgets inline in the Antigravity chat or as standalone Antigravity artifacts. Use when running inside Antigravity and you want to show the user diagrams, data visualizations, interactive controls, or educational walkthroughs beyond plain markdown. In other hosts (e.g. Claude Code / claude.ai) prefer that host's own artifact or page tooling.

skills.name: migrate-workflows
skills.description: Google Antigravity (agy): automatically migrate deprecated legacy workflow files (.agents/workflows/*.md, _agents/workflows/*.md, and global workflow folders) into modern skills (skills/NAME/SKILL.md), then safely archive the old files. Use when the user asks to migrate, convert, or upgrade workflows to skills, when legacy workflow files are found in a workspace, or when the user types /migrate-workflows.

skills.name: permissioned-github
skills.description: Google Antigravity (agy) sandbox rules for the gh CLI and git: which commands are allowed by default, and how to request extra permissions from the user when a gh/git command fails because of agent-environment restrictions. Use when running gh or git inside Antigravity, when a GitHub operation is denied or blocked by the sandbox, or before pushing, opening PRs, or calling the GitHub API from an Antigravity agent. Defer to the host's own GitHub rules when not running in Antigravity.

skills.name: plugin
skills.description: Google Antigravity (agy) only: how to manage and create Antigravity plugins — namespaced bundles of skills, agents, rules, MCP servers and hooks under ~/.gemini/config/plugins that install, enable and disable as one unit. Use when the user, in Antigravity, wants to enable, disable, install or uninstall a plugin, create a new plugin, or package a customization as a plugin, or types /plugin. Not for Claude Code plugins/marketplaces, and not for the underlying customization system (discovery roots, loading priority, standalone skills/rules/hooks) — see agy-customizations for that.

skills.name: run-workflow
skills.description: Google Antigravity (agy) only: how to write and run a dynamic workflow script with Antigravity's run_workflow tool — a Python script that orchestrates many agents with agent, parallel, pipeline, and phase. Use when the run_workflow tool is available and a task splits into many independent or staged pieces of agent work (fan out over files, modules, bugs, or review angles, then aggregate), or when the user asks for a workflow. Don't use for a single delegated task (use a subagent), when run_workflow is not available, or for legacy workflow files (see migrate-workflows).

skills.name: ui-plugin-navigation
skills.description: Google Antigravity (agy) only: discover UI plugin panels relevant to the current task and surface a one-click pill in the Antigravity chat to open (toggle) them in the side pane. Use when a running Antigravity UI plugin's panel would help with what the user is doing, or right after the user enables a new UI plugin pane and a shortcut to open it is handy.

backend-cloud.title: Cloud, Database & Backend Architecture
backend-cloud.description: High-performance APIs, database optimization, cloud primitives, microservices, and security.

skills.name: neon
skills.description: Overview of Neon, a complete set of cloud backend primitives for apps and agents, spanning Lakebase Postgres, Auth, the Data API, Object Storage, Compute Functions, and the AI Gateway. Start here to route to the right Neon skill, set up the CLI or MCP server, and follow the branch-first workflow. Use when "Neon" or "Lakebase Postgres" is mentioned, or when any of its individual capabilities are the trigger: "object storage" or "S3", "buckets", "serverless functions", "AI gateway", "call an LLM", "logs", "branch logs", "query logs", "log export", "Loki", "Grafana", "observability", "telemetry", "postgres", "database", or "backend". Also use when there is no Neon account yet, the user cannot sign in or provide an API key right now and needs a project they can claim later, or the user asks for a throwaway DATABASE_URL, Claimable Neon, Claimable Postgres, neon.new, claimable.neon.tech, instant Postgres, a no-signup database, temporary postgres, quick postgres, a no credit card database, or npx neon-new.

skills.name: neon-postgres
skills.description: Guides and best practices for working with Lakebase Postgres, the database behind Neon. Covers setup, connection methods and drivers, pooled vs direct connections, branching, schema migrations, autoscaling, scale-to-zero, instant restore, read replicas, connection pooling, IP allow lists, and logical replication. Also covers Lakebase Search: semantic vector search, full-text search with BM25 ranking, and hybrid search. Use when users ask about "Lakebase Postgres", "Neon setup", "connect to Neon", "Neon project", "DATABASE_URL", "serverless Postgres", "Neon CLI", "neon", "Neon MCP", "Neon Auth", "@neondatabase/serverless", "@neondatabase/neon-js", "scale to zero", "Neon autoscaling", "Neon read replica", "Neon connection pooling", "schema migrations", "database troubleshooting", "Postgres performance", "neon inspect db", "semantic search", "vector search", "full-text search", "BM25", or "hybrid search".
